note: Thursday 07:00 SGT sweep, pre-Asia-open (SGX 09:00, HKEX 09:30), after the Wed 22 Jul US close — levels/quotes are as of that close unless noted. Fresh items (7 of 14) are dated 22 Jul; the rest are decision-relevant items from 8-21 Jul. The dominant cross-portfolio driver stays the escalating US-Iran / Strait of Hormuz war premium feeding oil and precious metals while keeping the Fed hawkish into the 28-29 Jul FOMC. Every item source-verified against the cited pages.

items.headline: Silver climbs to ~$59.5/oz Wednesday as war premium and oil feed inflation-hedge demand
items.summary: September silver futures opened near $59.09 on Wed 22 July and rose to roughly $59.4-$59.6/oz intraday, up ~1.1-1.2% on the day, extending Tuesday's ~4% rip. Gains were driven by ongoing Middle East uncertainty and rising oil prices feeding safe-haven and inflation-hedge demand. Silver remains roughly 50% below its late-January record near $121.
items.actionable: Directly positive for the levered silver + silver-miner sleeve — the two-day bounce puts the metal firmly back above $58, but the driver is the war/inflation premium, not a rates thaw. Treat strength as a chance to right-size leverage into next week's FOMC rather than confirmation of a new leg; a Hormuz de-escalation would deflate it fast.

items.headline: Brent tops $94 (highest since June) on an 11th night of US strikes on Iran; Hormuz traffic near standstill
items.summary: Brent crude surged ~4% above $94/bbl and WTI rose ~3% to ~$86.85 on Wed 22 July after an 11th consecutive night of US strikes on Iranian military facilities. Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz — which carries ~one-fifth of global oil — has largely stalled, and US average gasoline climbed back above $4/gallon.
items.actionable: Bullish for the energy sleeve and for precious metals via the war premium, but the same oil spike feeds the inflation impulse that keeps the Fed hawkish — a headwind for HK tech, rate-sensitive S-REITs and levered silver longer-term. Trade the de-escalation risk, not the individual legs.

items.headline: Gold rebounds ~1.8% to ~$4,152/oz, still ~28% below its January record
items.summary: Gold rose ~1.8% on 22 July to about $4,151/oz, from near $4,054 the prior session, joining the risk/safe-haven bid. The metal remains roughly 28% below its 29 Jan 2026 intraday record (~$5,595) but is still up ~22% year-on-year. Miners lag bullion on cost inflation, with GDX around $74 (down ~14% YTD).
items.actionable: $4,000 held and gold is back above $4,150 — relief for GDX/SLVP after their washout. A clean reclaim of the spring highs would signal the miners' correction is done; a fade back toward $4,000 keeps them on watch. Real rates and next week's FOMC remain the arbiter.

items.headline: Lynas shares hit five-month low after Q4 revenue MISS — the ex-China rare-earth bellwether disappoints
items.summary: Lynas Rare Earths (LYC.AX) fell to a five-month low after Q4 (to 30 June) sales of A$288.9m (+9% y/y) badly missed the ~A$391m consensus, with rare-earth sales volumes declining in the quarter. Lynas is the largest producer of separated rare-earth oxides outside China; the miss lands after a ~63% three-month run on the China export-curb re-rate.
items.actionable: Near-term negative read-through for the whole ex-China rare-earth watchlist (LYC, MP, USAR, UUUU) on volume/pricing softness — the sell-the-news risk flagged yesterday materialized. The strategic supply-security thesis is intact, so treat basket weakness as watch-and-wait, not an automatic add; the China-incumbent counter-bet 6680.HK is relatively insulated.

items.headline: US intensifies Iran campaign to protect Hormuz shipping; tanker hit, traffic near standstill
items.summary: The US said mid-July strikes on Iran aimed to protect vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, hitting an oil tanker near Iran's main export terminal as strait traffic slumped. President Trump is weighing whether to expand the campaign; the crisis began 28 Feb 2026. Brent has held a firm risk premium above $90 throughout.
items.actionable: The escalating war premium is the single biggest cross-portfolio driver right now — bullish oil and precious metals, but it hardens the Fed's higher-for-longer stance that pressures HK tech, S-REITs and risk assets. Keep position sizing that survives headline whipsaw in both directions; a ceasefire would sharply reverse the metals/oil bid and relieve the rate premium.

items.headline: Fed seen holding at 3.50-3.75% on 28-29 July (~80%) under hawkish Chair Warsh; committee split
items.summary: Markets price ~80% odds of no change at the 28-29 July FOMC, keeping the funds rate at 3.50-3.75%, with Chair Kevin Warsh stressing the 2% target is not yet met. The 17 June minutes showed officials evenly split — roughly half favoring holds/cuts and half favoring a hike before year-end — and the oil spike has kept September-hike risk alive.
items.actionable: The dominant macro headwind for the book's highest-beta pain point (levered silver + gold miners) and for S-REITs stays higher-for-longer with a live hike tail, not cuts. The big USD cash pile keeps earning ~3.5-3.75% as productive dry powder; a dovish 29 July surprise would be a sharp positive catalyst for metals and HK tech.

items.headline: S&P 500 hits record ~7,509 as earnings beats offset the Iran war; Alphabet, Tesla, IBM due this week
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.89% to a record ~7,509 and the Nasdaq gained 1.29% to ~25,837 on Tue 21 July, led by chipmakers, as ~88% of the ~66 S&P names reporting so far beat EPS (3M +7%, GM +5%). Micron, Sandisk and AMD led a memory-chip surge. Alphabet, IBM and Tesla report later this week.
items.actionable: A risk-on US tape and semis rebound are a supportive read-through for HK-tech beta (SMIC 0981, the Tencent book) and crypto, but the concentration in mega-cap earnings this week means an Alphabet/Tesla miss could reverse sentiment quickly — earnings-contingent, not confirmed.

items.headline: Hong Kong tech rallies as Alibaba, Tencent lead on AI and Apple Intelligence approval with Qwen
items.summary: Chinese stocks in Hong Kong jumped the most in 14 months in early July, with Alibaba up ~11% and Tencent up ~3% on AI-chip optimism. Alibaba previewed its 2.4-trillion-parameter Qwen3.8 Max, and Apple Intelligence won Chinese regulatory approval in mid-July with Alibaba's Qwen designated the foundational model for the localized experience.
items.actionable: Constructive momentum for the HK-tech basket (Tencent, Alibaba, Meituan, Xiaomi) on AI monetization plus the 'national team' policy put. Xiaomi still lags (~-34% YTD) so it offers relative catch-up if the rally broadens; watch Alibaba's actual earnings and late-July Politburo fiscal follow-through for confirmation.

items.headline: Singapore STI hits record ~5,561 as DBS, OCBC, UOB rally into Q2 earnings; Seatrium reports 24 July
items.summary: The Straits Times Index touched an all-time high of 5,561 on 15 July and delivered a ~21% total return through mid-July, led by DBS, OCBC and UOB reaching record levels. Banks rallied ahead of the early-August Q2 earnings season; DBS, Singtel and CapitaLand Ascendas REIT are among the largest 2026 retail net inflows. Seatrium reports 24 July, DBS Q2 in early August.
items.actionable: Positive for the SGX blue-chip sleeve (DBS, Singtel, CapitaLand REITs), but records into earnings raise the bar — Seatrium on 24 July and DBS Q2 in early August are the near-term catalysts for profit-taking risk. Higher-for-longer rates from the oil shock remain the S-REIT headwind.

items.headline: IEA warns China rare-earth curbs risk $6.5 trillion of downstream global production; Nov 10 suspension expiry looms
items.summary: The IEA said full implementation of China's rare-earth export curbs could jeopardize $6.5 trillion in downstream production outside China, with the US and Europe accounting for nearly half the exposure. China's April 2025 restrictions on seven elements remain in place, a 1 July 2026 public reporting mechanism signals tighter enforcement, and a suspension of expanded controls expires 10 Nov 2026.
items.actionable: Reinforces the structural supply-security thesis behind the ex-China rare-earth watchlist even after Lynas' weak print. The 10 Nov suspension expiry is the key catalyst date that could re-rate MP, Lynas and USAR if China lets curbs snap back — a multi-quarter thesis to accumulate on weakness, not chase.

items.headline: June CPI cools to 3.5% headline as energy plunges; core eases to 2.6%
items.summary: Headline CPI fell 0.4% m/m in June — the biggest monthly drop in over six years — cutting annual inflation to 3.5% vs 3.8% expected, as the energy index dropped 5.7% on the month. Core CPI was flat m/m, pulling the annual core rate to 2.6%, below the 2.9% consensus. The feared hot core did not materialize.
items.actionable: A genuinely soft disinflation print supports the eventual-cuts case and a softer USD — positive for gold/silver and EM/HK tech, mildly negative for the cash pile's real yield. But June's energy plunge predates July's oil spike and will likely reverse in the next print, which is exactly why the Fed stays hawkish.

items.headline: Bitcoin hovers near $66k, Ether ~$1,940, Solana ~$78 as crypto opens higher then fades
items.summary: Bitcoin opened ~$66,509 on 22 July, about 2% above Tuesday's open, but slipped to ~$65,859 by mid-morning ET. Ether traded near $1,943 and Solana near $78, with both majors losing early gains. BTC remains well below the Oct-2025 ATH (~$126k).
items.actionable: No direct holding, but crypto is range-bound and correlating with broad risk appetite rather than leading — a useful confirming barometer. A hawkish Fed hold on 29 July and the war premium are the swing factors; a sustained hold above ~$66k keeps the risk backdrop constructive, a break under ~$62.5k is the early risk-off tell.

items.headline: US dollar (DXY) eases to ~101 as war premium meets soft CPI and a hawkish Fed
items.summary: The DXY slipped to ~101.1 on 22 July, pulling back from a late-June peak near 101.4, caught between safe-haven demand from the Iran war and cooler June CPI. Warsh's hawkish tone provides support even as officials remain divided on the rate path; year-end Street forecasts drift toward ~98.
items.actionable: A range-bound-to-softer dollar is mildly negative for the USD cash pile's purchasing power but supportive for gold, silver and HK/Asian equities. A decisive break below ~100 would strengthen the precious-metals and EM case; the war premium is currently capping the downside.

items.headline: Energy Fuels ramps US rare-earth push: $1.9B VAC deal, $725M Pentagon backing, CEO insider buy
items.summary: Energy Fuels (UUUU) announced a $1.9B acquisition of magnet maker Vacuumschmelze (23 June) and a conditional commitment for up to $725M in senior-secured debt from the US Office of Strategic Capital (18 June) to expand US rare-earth and critical-materials capacity. CEO Ross Bhappy bought 74,000 shares (~$968K) on 7 July; the 52-week range is $8.16-$27.90.
items.actionable: US-government-backed vertical integration plus insider buying strengthen the domestic rare-earth/magnet thesis for the UUUU/USAR/MP watchlist, cushioning the Lynas-miss read-through. Analysts stay cautious (Roth PT $16, Neutral) — a name to accumulate on weakness rather than chase.
